correctness.rationale: Exact signed-trace criterion follows by contracting required-equality edges, properly coloring the quotient negative graph and splitting color classes to exactly q. Forest necessity follows from a cycle label contradiction; global cardinality necessity follows from the all-positive labeling. For forests of at most n-q edges every contracted negative graph is a forest, hence 2-colorable with at least q contracted vertices, giving sufficiency. Graphic-matroid truncation and Tutte forest expansion give exact VC rank/polynomial; Cayley and exponential formula count facets on K_n. For q=3, all-negative traces encode ordinary 3-colorability; NP membership is immediate. All hypotheses and q=1,q=n boundaries were checked. The provided verifier completed 9916 support/q cases plus trace and exchange checks; finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: Exact number of nonempty blocks is a natural fixed-k clustering constraint in same-cluster learning. The result identifies *every* shattered query support on *any* available query graph as a graphic-matroid truncation, giving a linear-time recognition algorithm, sharp VC dimension, a Tutte-based all-face polynomial, and pure facets. The full signed-trace theorem simultaneously exposes a sharp structural contrast: individual trace feasibility for three blocks is NP-complete, while universal shattering is linear-time. These are natural global and graph-restricted invariants not supplied by a simple cardinality bound, and the theorem has potential use in hypothesis-capacity estimates.
